source: Matt Croom's audit of the Daily Internal Compliance 2026 workbook — monthly review received 10/1/2026 (supersedes all earlier September versions), YTD reports received 9/30/2026
method: Completion % = Yes ÷ (Yes + No). Day forms, trailer inspection and trailer readiness are credited to the day tech; night forms to the night tech.

month.label: September 2026

concerns.t: Night forms are the weakest area and getting worse
concerns.d: 40.3% in September, down from 55.4% in August. ETX nights: 6 of 31 (19.4%). Mitsui nights: 2 of 26 (7.7%) — almost all on Marcos Morales's shifts (he completed 1 of 19).

concerns.t: Trailer readiness is slipping — and it's almost entirely XTO
concerns.d: XTO was 149 of 219 (68.0%) and accounts for 70 of the 72 readiness misses, spread across many different techs. A crew-wide habit, not one or two names.

concerns.t: Supervision jobs are well behind air jobs
concerns.d: Supervision: day forms 68.2%, night forms 38.6%. Air jobs: day forms 96.0%.
Ovintiv 28 of 48 (58.3%) · Diamondback 53 of 76 (69.7%) · Comstock 30 of 41 (73.2%) · SM Energy 81.9% with night forms at 62.5%.

ytd.label: 2026 Year-to-Date (Jan 1 – Sep 30)
ytd.note: 273 daily tabs, 13,595 job-days. Only about half of job-days were audited YTD — and fewer than a third before June — so these are misses that were FOUND, not every miss.
standouts: Night forms have fallen from ~89% in January to 44% in September. Trailer readiness has fallen too — from nearly 100% through May to ~70% since June.
By customer: XTO has the highest day-form rate at 95%. Ovintiv (66%) and Southwest Operating (55%) have the lowest.
Coverage rose above 90% in July and August, then dropped to 55% in September — early-month percentages rest on small samples.
ytd.followUp: Techs with 40+ day shifts under 70% on day forms YTD: Benjamin Boutte (33%), Wesley Bertrand (36%), Michael Slaydon (40%), Allen White (55%), Josh Blassingame (57%), Marcos Morales (62%), BJ Caesar (62%).
